sources.title: Stock price jumps: news and volume play a minor role
sources.verification_status: selected original text inspected; no raw-data replication
sources.definition: Absolute one-minute return exceeds s times 120-minute mean absolute return; s=4 reported count. Not four standard deviations.
limitations: Stock denominator is internally inconsistent; exact independent normalized rate not established.
Repeated minute flags are not distinct harmful or actionable episodes.
Historical restricted sample; no Project 50K threshold validation.
PDF prints November 26, 2024 although arXiv v1 metadata is March 12, 2008; discrepancy preserved.
Inspected text specifies a 120-minute flat moving average but does not establish one-sided/trailing orientation.
sources.causal_status: Liquidity micro-crisis interpretation is conjectural; no incidence of verified causes measured.

sources.title: Understanding temporal dynamics of jumps in cryptocurrency markets: evidence from tick-by-tick data
sources.verification_status: publisher selected text and exact Table 4 inspected; no tick-data replication

sections_read_selected: 5.2 Crypto market microstructure and jump testing

sources.unit: detected econometric jumps; eligible test days
sources.definition: Lee-Mykland noise-adjusted moment detections accepted only on days also passing Ait-Sahalia-Jacod-Li jump test, with multiple-testing adjustment and eligibility filters.
sources.denominator: Per-currency eligible test days after sampling/completeness filters, not all calendar days or all cryptocurrencies.

observed.safe_ratio_unit: detected jumps per 100 eligible test days

limitations: Introduction describes 58%/32% of days; Table 4 numerator is N jumps. Distinct jump-date counts not reconciled here; do not convert event/day ratio to probability.
Eligibility excludes incomplete/illiquid asset-days; aggregation and microstructure affect detection.
Historical econometric events do not measure usefulness, causes, fraud or local detector incidence.
